thread_text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO p99 breach detected on continuous-batching streaming path in us-west-2. Alerting 3 customers (customer-A, customer-B, customer-C). p95 ~110ms, p99 ~2.4s; streaming stalls observed. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/contbatch-streaming. Escalate to eng-oncall.

alice_oncall: seeing the same in dashboards — p99 spike started ~5m ago and correlates with a surge in batch pack sizes. Packet: <https://metrics/usw2/contbatch/pack_size>.

ben_sre: joining. can you confirm if any recent deploys hit packer or batcher in last 30m? ops-bot, what changed?

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports a config change 18m ago: batcher.max_pack_size increased from 12 -> 20 in us-west-2 by carla_engineer (PR #4921).

carla_engineer: yep that was the tiny throughput optimization for high-seqlen jobs; suggested to ops to flip on for us-west canary. I didn't anticipate streaming stalls.

alice_oncall: logs show many streaming sessions stuck in "awaiting-kv" state for >1.5s. snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T18:02:31Z] session=abcd stream_id=1234 state=awaiting-kv kv_hits=0 pack_size=18 wait_ms=1520
[2026-03-15T18:02:32Z] session=efgh stream_id=5678 state=executing kv_hits=1 pack_size=19 latency_ms=58
```

ben_sre: that aligns — packing bigger batches increases KV cache lookup contention and causes some sessions to wait on remote memory/paging. Risk amplifies for mixed sequence-length workloads.

dave_prod: customer-A reported degraded UX (partial streams, long hangs). Support ticket: https://redwood/tickets/3421. We need quick mitigation and customer comms.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan (quick wins): 1) revert batcher.max_pack_size to 12 for us-west-2, 2) enable pack-shed-preemptive=true, 3) route streaming traffic for top 3 customers to fallback smaller model instance pool for 30m. I can run these.

carla_engineer: I can patch the config now. command I will run: ```sh
# revert max pack size
curl -XPOST "https://ops-api.usw2.redwood/configs/batcher" -d '{"max_pack_size":12}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
# enable preemptive shed
curl -XPOST "https://ops-api.usw2.redwood/configs/batcher" -d '{"preemptive_shed":true}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

elena_support: pinging customer-A + B to let them know we're investigating; will note possible partial streams and SLO blips.

ben_sre: before we revert, can we snapshot current metrics and tracing so postmortem has context? run: ```sh
curl "https://metrics-api.usw2.redwood/query?metric=contbatch.pack_size&from=-10m&to=now" > /tmp/pack_size.json
kubectl logs -n contbatch -l app=batcher --tail=500 > /tmp/batcher_tail.log
```

alice_oncall: done with snapshots, uploading to incident channel.

carla_engineer: applying revert now. ```sh
# apply revert via ops-api
curl -s -XPOST "https://ops-api.usw2.redwood/configs/batcher" -d '{"max_pack_size":12, "preemptive_shed":true}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' && echo done
```

ops-bot: config update acknowledged. rollout started to us-west-2 batcher fleet (gradual: 15% -> 50% -> 100%).

~3m later~

alice_oncall: metrics update: p99 dropped from 2.4s -> 520ms after 50% rollout. Streaming stalls reduced significantly. p95 unchanged.

ben_sre: good. we should still route critical customer streaming sessions away from heavy-seqlen hosts for safety. carla, can you apply a routing policy to pin customer-A/B/C to fallback-pool?

carla_engineer: routing policy applied: ```json
{"routing": {"customer_ids": ["customer-A","customer-B","customer-C"], "pool": "fallback-small-pack"}}
```

ben_sre: verify trace for a recently affected session. trace id: trace-0f9c. It shows KV eviction spike at token 1200, pack_size 18, and a wait loop before execution. This is consistent with paging pressure on the fast KV layer.

alice_oncall: I'm leaving mitigation in place and will monitor for 20m. Handing off to ben_sre for overnight watch and follow-ups. TODOs for handoff: - keep preemptive_shed=true, - keep max_pack_size=12 in us-west-2 for now, - create postmortem + root cause (pack_size tuning + lack of seqlen-aware scheduler), - triage PR #4921 for regressions and add canary test for streaming stalls.

ben_sre: taking it. I'll keep an eye and escalate if p99 > 1s for >5m or customer tickets escalate. Also tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml to look at smarter decision: seqlen-aware batching and kv-reservation.

dave_prod: I'll coordinate customer comms: update tickets with mitigation and ETA for postmortem.

elena_support: customers notified with courtesy status update. No immediate escalations yet.

carla_engineer: quick follow-up note: PR #4921 intended to improve throughput on long-sequence offline workloads; we should gate that change behind a mixed-workload canary. Adding test plan to PR now.

ben_sre: recorded all artifacts: /incidents/7070001110/artifacts (metrics, logs, traces, patch diff). Assigning postmortem owner: carla_engineer. Deadline: draft by EOD tomorrow.

alice_oncall: thanks team. moving to monitoring-only. If anything flares, ping @ben_sre and @alice_oncall. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev3. Customers affected: customer-A, customer-B, customer-C. Next steps: postmortem, additional canary tests, seqlen-aware scheduler RFC.
